summary.headline: Tuesday read, first real session since Friday 8/14 close (Monday 8/17 traded but pre-market drops both days showed stale prices; today's drop finally reflects Monday's move). Broad macro backdrop: Brent crude above $91/bbl, 30-year Treasury yields at their highest since 2007, and Middle East geopolitical risk pushed futures lower into the open -- this is pressuring the Dividend sleeve broadly (CHD -3.28%, ADP -2.52%, LMT -2.40%, QCOM -2.23%, SYK -2.08%, SSNC -2.06%, CL -1.89%, GPC -1.84%), none with company-specific bad news (ADP and LMT both carry recent price-target raises and in-line-or-better fundamentals) -- reading as rate-driven multiple compression, not thesis deterioration, capped as a single AMBER macro flag rather than eight individual RED calls. MARA and EIX persist RED (thesis-confirmed): MARA +5.54% today on 'upbeat guidance' optimism (board refresh, expected HPC/data-center lease deals per Morgan Stanley) but Cantor/Clear Street still cut price targets below the current price and the BTC-leverage/GAAP-loss thesis is unchanged; EIX -0.18% (calm) but the Aug-31 wildfire-liability-reform deadline is now 13 days out -- CEO Pizarro still hasn't seen draft legislation, though Newsom is pushing a last-minute liability-capping package and a judge tentatively denied one wildfire liability claim against SCE, both incrementally favorable but nothing resolved. FTNT persists AMBER, now down 4 straight sessions on valuation/multiple-compression concern even as billings actually accelerated to +33% YoY in Q2 -- fundamentals intact, price still working through the correction. TOL reports Q3 earnings today after the close (call Wednesday) -- consensus $2.93 EPS/$2.62B revenue, shares -1.83% into the print on the same rate-sensitivity concern driving the broader Dividend-sleeve pullback. Notable gainers: CRDO +8.87% and MRVL +5.47%, both squarely on their own AI-infrastructure/hyperscaler-capex key_catalysts (1.6T networking transition, new AI memory infrastructure products); DVN +3.78% on continued strong Coterra-integration execution (guidance tightened and beaten, $1.25B 2026 debt-reduction target already completed, Solitude Pipeline FID) -- its own key_risk (integration/guidance-visibility risk) is trending the opposite direction from materializing. COIN, SUPV, and HOOD -- AMBER since 8/15 -- all resolve to GREEN: COIN +1.43%, SUPV -0.87% (essentially flat, no news), HOOD +0.72%, no fresh negative catalysts on any. New AMBER calendar watch: MRVL reports Q2 FY2027 results 8/28 after close. CWAN roster-integrity bug hits a 50th consecutive day (PR #11/#12 still open/unmerged/dirty) -- see roster_integrity. SPY sits ~19.7% above the one active support level (645.80) -- not in play.

flags.headline: +5.54% on guidance optimism, but BTC-leverage/GAAP-loss thesis unchanged and PTs still below spot
flags.detail: MARA rallied to $9.71 (+5.54%) on renewed optimism around its energy/HPC strategic pivot -- a refreshed board with two independent directors and Morgan Stanley flagging at least one high-performance-computing lease deal plus two Starwood JV site leases expected by year-end. But analyst price targets remain well below the current price (Morgan Stanley raised to just $6 from $5.50; Cantor Fitzgerald cut to $12 from $14; Clear Street cut to $10 from $12, Hold), and the underlying Q2 thesis -- a $611M net loss on a 27% revenue miss, driven by BTC mark-to-market volatility and $850M of convertible debt obligations -- is unchanged. No new fundamental data since the Q2 print.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Persistent GAAP losses ($1.3B in Q1 2026 alone) driven by Bitcoin price volatility and mark-to-market accounting create existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn and the company cannot service its $850M convertible debt obligations.'

flags.headline: Aug-31 wildfire-reform deadline 13 days out; Newsom pushes late package, judge sides with SCE in one case -- still unresolved
flags.detail: CEO Pizarro's warning stands: as of this run, Edison still hasn't seen draft wildfire-liability-reform legislation, and the state legislative session (which reconvened Aug 3 after summer recess) ends Aug 31 -- 13 days out. Two incrementally favorable but non-dispositive developments since the last check: Gov. Newsom is pushing a last-minute package that would cap attorneys' fees and limit local-government/victim recoveries (would reduce utility liability exposure if it passes); and a Superior Court judge tentatively denied a request to hold SCE automatically liable for a wildfire under the state's inverse-condemnation standard. Neither resolves the core credit-downgrade risk -- that hinges on whether any bill actually passes in the next two weeks. Shares calm, -0.18% at $71.30.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'Elevated debt-to-equity of 216% amplifies financial risk from future wildfire events, adverse rate case outcomes, or rising interest rates... California's complex regulatory and political environment creates uncertainty around cost recovery, rate base returns, and wildfire liability frameworks.'

evidence.source: Claims Journal (judge denies SCE strict-liability claim)

flags.headline: -2.61% today, 4th consecutive down session -- valuation/multiple compression, not fundamentals
flags.detail: FTNT fell to $155.79 (-2.61%), its fourth straight down session since the Q2 print. This is the market working through valuation, not a fundamentals problem: billings actually accelerated to +33% YoY ($2.37B) with product revenue up 52% in Q2, and guidance was raised. Analyst commentary since the print has focused on the stock's elevated multiple (~29x forward P/E, 27% above the $113.78 consensus PT) and the risk of deceleration once the current firewall-refresh cycle crests -- carrying at AMBER, not escalating, consistent with prior runs.
flags.thesis_link: Matches FTNT key_risk: 'Stock trades 27% above consensus analyst price target of $113.78 -- any deceleration in billings growth from 31% could trigger significant multiple compression from the current 29x forward P/E.' (Billings growth has not decelerated -- this is multiple compression on valuation concern, not the risk fully materializing.)

flags.headline: Broad Dividend-sleeve pullback on rising long-end yields and oil-driven inflation fear, not stock-specific news
flags.detail: Eight Dividend-sleeve names moved -1.8% to -3.3% today with no company-specific negative catalyst found for any: CHD -3.28%, ADP -2.52%, LMT -2.40%, QCOM -2.23%, SYK -2.08%, SSNC -2.06%, CL -1.89%, GPC -1.84%. The common driver is macro: Brent crude above $91/bbl reviving inflation concern, 30-year Treasury yields at their highest since 2007, and Middle East geopolitical risk pushing futures lower (S&P -0.41%, Nasdaq -0.76% pre-market). ADP and LMT both carry recent price-target raises and in-line-or-better fundamentals (ADP beat Q4 revenue and guided FY2027 higher; LMT posted a record $230B backlog and raised guidance last quarter) -- this reads as rate-sensitive multiple compression across the sleeve, not a thesis event on any single name. Watching for persistence tomorrow before treating any individual name as its own flag.

flags.headline: +3.78%, Coterra integration executing well -- key_risk trending opposite of materializing
flags.detail: DVN rose to $47.58 (+3.78%). This directly counters the roster's own flagged integration/guidance-visibility key_risk on the Coterra merger -- worth noting explicitly as a risk that is not materializing, six weeks after the previous run's tracking of this name.
flags.thesis_link: DVN key_risk: 'Reported revenue growth... is a merger-consolidation artifact... once the Coterra deal anniversaries in mid-2027, headline growth comparisons will normalize.' Integration execution to date (synergies ahead of schedule, debt targets met early, guidance beaten and tightened) is running counter to this risk, not confirming it.
